query: What node‑hour and wall‑time ranges are typical for PBE0/HSE06 DFT+SOC, GW/BSE, TDDFT+SOC, and DFPT phonon runs on ~100–300 atom cluster models?

response.query: What node‑hour and wall‑time ranges are typical for PBE0/HSE06 DFT+SOC, GW/BSE, TDDFT+SOC, and DFPT phonon runs on ~100–300 atom cluster models?
response.answer: PBE0/HSE06 DFT+SOC, GW/BSE, TDDFT+SOC, and DFPT phonon runs on ~100–300 atom clusters typically require 100–1000 node-hours and 1–10 wall-clock days. Computational demands vary with method complexity and system size.

results.content: Moreover, to explicitly include finite temperature and pressure effects by means of dynamical sampling methods, analytical gradients are generally available for all classical and QM electronic structure methods, even in combination with PBCs. This is made possible by the Quickstep module, (14,22,23);) which is based on the Gaussian and plane wave (GPW) method and its all-electron counterpart denoted as the Gaussian and augmented plane wave (GAPW) approach, (24,25);) and contains all electronic structure methods described in Section 2, i.e. in particular DFT and Hartree–Fock (HF), (26);) but also hybrid-DFT and post-HF schemes such as second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) (27);) and the random phase approximation (RPA). The unique aspect of the GPW and GAPW methods is their usage of a mixed Gaussian and an auxiliary plane wave (PW) basis set, thereby unifying the computational efficiency of a compact localized basis set with the simplicity of PWs for periodic electronic structure calculations.
